title: File menu has no 'New Project'
wanted: start a new project for my ski footage, since I'm on a practice project
did: opened File menu
happened: File menu offers Import…, Import from Media Browser…, Open bin or cut…, Index…, Project Settings…, Export… — nothing called New Project / New. The words 'bin' and 'cut' are used instead of project, so I can't tell if 'Open bin or cut…' is how you make a new one.
expected: File > New Project… (every editor I've used has it)
suggestion: Add File > New project… that asks for a name and a footage folder

title: Tour never says how to start your own project
wanted: the tour to tell me how to put MY footage in a fresh project
did: read all 6 tour steps
happened: Step 1 'Bring in footage' says add more clips to this Project panel with File › Import; nothing about a new project, and nothing says what 'bin' or 'cut' mean although the title bar uses them ('starter-bin main'). The tour also appeared a second or two late, after I had already clicked File, and opened on top of the menu.
suggestion: Make tour step 1 'Start your film: pick your footage folder' and explain bin = project, cut = version

title: Help menu has only the tour and the shortcut list
wanted: Help to answer 'how do I start a new project with my folder?'
did: opened Help
happened: Help has two items: 'Learn Roughcut…' (the same 6-step tour) and 'Keyboard shortcuts'. No search, no topics, no 'getting started', nothing about bins/cuts/projects.
suggestion: A short Help page with 'Start a new film from a folder' as the first topic, or a searchable Help that also searches menu commands

title: Making a new project is hidden in the title dropdown as a typed path
wanted: start a new project with my Copper folder
did: looked in File (no New), Help (no topic), then clicked the 'starter-bin main ▾' label in the title bar
happened: The only way I found is a text field at the bottom of that dropdown: 'open a folder… (its path, typed or pasted)', under a heading 'BINS'. There is no folder picker / Browse button, and nothing calls it a new project. I only found it by clicking a label that looks like a title. A CapCut/iMovie person would not guess 'bin' = project, nor know the full path of their footage.
expected: a 'New project from folder…' button with a Browse dialog, visible on the empty screen
suggestion: Put 'New film from a folder…' in File and on the empty timeline card, with a folder browser

title: Cost line '~$0.26 API-equivalent · free on your plan' is puzzling
wanted: know whether running the AI costs me money
did: read the title dropdown
happened: It shows a dollar figure and 'free on your plan' together. As a newcomer I don't know what 'API-equivalent' means or what plan I'm on; seeing a $ amount next to the AI makes me hesitate even though it says free.
suggestion: Say just 'Included in your plan' and hide the API figure behind a details link

title: Index panel opens full of jargon on a new project
wanted: understand what the screen is showing me after opening my footage
did: opened my folder; the Index tab came up by itself
happened: Columns 'Heard / Looked / Close / Telemetry / Preview / Local (3080) / Cost / Ran', a 'Look' dropdown, 'every 4 s', and 'Hybrid (3080 + Claude)'. 'The 3080 scans for free; Claude double-checks only what the cut uses.' I don't know what a 3080 is or which of these I'm supposed to touch; it reads like an engineer's control panel, and I can't see thumbnails of my clips here.
suggestion: On a fresh project show the clips as thumbnails (Project tab) and keep Index for later; replace '3080' with 'this computer'

title: 'Run first pass' says what and what it costs, but not how long
wanted: know before I start whether this is 1 minute or 1 hour
did: hovered Run first pass
happened: Rich tooltip: 'Hears and looks at every clip…', COST 'free on your Claude plan — about $36.04 estimated cost if using the API', CHANGES 'Nothing until you accept'. No time estimate at all. Also the $36.04 here vs '~$0.26' in the title dropdown on the practice project — big scary number on a hover.
suggestion: Add 'about N minutes for 26 clips (31 min of footage)' to the tooltip

title: One clip shows sideways/tall in Source but landscape on its thumbnail

happened: The poster thumbnail is a normal wide picture of a ceiling with lights; in the Source monitor the same clip is a narrow tall picture with everything turned 90° (faces sideways). title: The proposed cut is 2:56 and there was nowhere to tell it my length first

expected: a 'How long? 30s / 1 min / 2 min / 3 min' choice before running

title: One misclick on Discard throws away the whole 18-shot proposed cut, no confirm, and Undo says 'nothing to undo'
